description: Versioned machine-readable contract for the Harvest management API. Update this file and CHANGELOG.md whenever a route is added, removed, renamed, or its request/response shape changes.

breaking_changes: Changing the type of a response field
Renaming a route (path or method change)
Changing a query parameter from optional to required
Adding a new mutating route without classifying it in this contract
non_breaking_changes: Adding a new optional response field
Adding a new optional query parameter
Adding a new optional request body field
Narrowing an existing error response to be more specific

auth_note: Route authorization posture is classified in issue #174. This contract records the route surface and category; auth enforcement is separate.
audit_note: Mutating routes (read_only: false) are covered by the audit trail (issue #158). The audit endpoint itself is read-only.

routes.description: Atomically start a workflow if no live run for (workflow_name, workflow_id) exists, or signal the existing run otherwise (issue #244). The signal lands deterministically before the workflow function is first dispatched on a fresh start, so first-tick author code observes it via the existing recv_signal / signal handler surface.
routes.idempotency: Idempotent on (workflow_name, workflow_id) per id_reuse_policy. When idempotency_key is supplied, repeated calls with the same (execution_id, idempotency_key) deliver the signal exactly once.

fields.name: workflow_id
fields.description: Stable identifier used to deduplicate concurrent starts.

fields.description: Workflow input payload applied only when a fresh execution is started.

fields.description: Signal channel name delivered to the execution (fresh or existing).

fields.name: signal_payload
fields.description: Signal payload (any JSON value). Defaults to null.

fields.description: Task queue name used only when a fresh execution is started.

fields.name: memo
fields.description: Non-indexed metadata (JSON object) used only when a fresh execution is started.

fields.name: search_attrs
fields.description: Indexed search attributes (JSON object) used only when a fresh execution is started.

fields.name: execution_timeout_secs
fields.description: Overall execution timeout in seconds, applied only on fresh start.

fields.name: id_reuse_policy
fields.description: Duplicate-id policy: allow_duplicate (default), reject_duplicate, allow_duplicate_failed_only, or terminate_if_running.

fields.name: idempotency_key
fields.description: Optional dedup key applied to the signal row; second call with the same key on the same execution is a no-op delivery (signal_delivered = false).

success_response.note: Returns 200 when an existing live execution is signaled rather than a fresh one started.

error_responses.description: Invalid request body, workflow name, or id_reuse_policy.

routes.description: Submit a synchronous update request to a running workflow. Blocks until admitted or completed depending on the wait parameter.

params.description: admitted — return when validated; completed — block until handler returns (default).

error_responses.description: Execution not found or update handler not registered.
Timed out waiting for completion (wait=completed exceeded the timeout).

routes.description: Poll the result of a previously admitted workflow update.

routes.description: Server-Sent Events stream of WorkflowEvent history for one execution. Emits every newly persisted event as id/event/data SSE messages. Resume via Last-Event-ID header. Closes with event:stream-end on terminal state. Keepalive :ping comments every 15 s (default). Returns 409 Conflict when Last-Event-ID implies more than buffer_depth events to replay (slow consumer).

headers.name: Last-Event-ID
headers.description: harvest_events.id BIGSERIAL cursor. When present, the server replays events with id > n before entering live-tail mode.

success_response.note: Content-Type: text/event-stream. Each SSE message carries id (BIGSERIAL), event (WorkflowEvent type name), and data (JSON event value). A final event:stream-end message signals terminal execution state. Returns 409 Conflict with {error:slow_consumer, drop_after_event_id} when the client is too far behind.

error_responses.description: Slow consumer: too many events to replay. Reconnect with Last-Event-ID: drop_after_event_id.
